title: structured output: add CFG + regex constrained decoding backends and tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: structured output support needs robust constrained decoding that works across model backends, streaming, and real-world tokenizers. This PR adds two new constrained-decoding backends (CFG/grammar backend and regex/tokenizer-aware backend), fixes tokenizer edge cases that caused constraint violations on unicode and multi-token punctuation, and wires the backends into the OpenAI-compatible API surface. Changes include runtime implementations, tests, docs, and light perf tuning. High-level changes: 1) new runtime/constrained_decoder/cfg_backend.* implementing a CFG-based constraint engine with streaming-friendly incremental parse checks; 2) new runtime/constrained_decoder/regex_tokenizer_backend.* that applies regex constraints at the tokenizer level and falls back to byte-level regex when token boundaries are ambiguous; 3) fixes to tokenizer/regex_utils.py to handle unicode combining marks and deprecated punctuation normalization that previously split logical characters across tokens; 4) API compatibility: accept new optional parameter constraints_backend=(cfg|regex|tokenizer) in the OpenAI-compat layer, defaulting to existing behavior; 5) extensive unit and integration tests under tests/structured_output and e2e tests that simulate streaming partial-token emissions; 6) docs update docs/api/structured-output.md and upgrade notes. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of CFG backend - [x] Regex/tokenizer backend with fallback - [x] Tokenizer fixes and new unit tests - [x] Integration tests for streaming + constraints - [x] Performance/regression benchmarks run (see notes) - [x] Documentation and API surface updated - [x] Reviewed and approved. Testing & CI: initial CI run showed a flaky integration test (e2e-streaming) due to timing on incremental parse checks; test adjusted to be resilient to small delays and rerun passed. Benchmarks: constrained decoding adds ~1-3% median token latency on CPU-backed models, negligible on GPU (0.5-1%), and increases success rate for strict CFG outputs from ~76% to ~98% in internal evals. Migration notes: default behavior unchanged; customers can opt-in by specifying constraints_backend. For Dedicated/Private deployments operators should ensure tokenizer versions are consistent across replicas (patch included to detect mismatches at startup).
